answer.rationale: Leadership pressure favors a price-matching response, but durable memory and the exp_73 archive both show targeted discounting drives short-term acquisition at the cost of 30-day retention, undermining sustainable qualified revenue—especially now that competitors are racing to the bottom on price. Instead, reinforcing the confirmed SMB-specific win (signup simplification lifting activation with negligible retention cost, memory_31) offers a lower-risk lever to retain price-sensitive accounts by improving perceived value and time-to-value rather than competing on price. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a plausible complementary lever but less directly tested against this SMB churn dynamic. Scaling as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) preserves the option to reassess given the competitive shock, and the promotional pricing risk is explicitly flagged for leadership rather than silently ruled out, since business pressure may still push toward a short-term price response despite known downstream harm.
